patch_description: Crossover combining the two programs: I keep the current program's stronger machinery (structured seeds — icosahedron+axis pairs, Fibonacci sphere, cube+center, antipodal pairs; ratio-aware log-sum-exp Adam smoothing of the true squared-distance ratio; exact SLSQP max-min refinement with diameter ≤ 1 constraints) and splice in the partner program's fast softmin gradient "spreading" preprocessor, which is used (a) to generate additional pre-conditioned random seeds before the Adam stage, and (b) as a cheap repulsion spreader. I then vectorize the SLSQP constraints (single array-valued constraint function with an analytic dense Jacobian built via fancy indexing instead of 182 separate Python closures), which makes each SLSQP call much faster, leaving budget for extra polish: alternating fine-tau Adam + SLSQP rounds plus noise-perturbation SLSQP restarts around the incumbent best. The final result is centered and normalized to diameter 1. The true objective (min(d²)/max(d²)) is what is tracked throughout, so any configuration that beats the reference squared ratio 1/4.1658 will push combined_score above 1. Fixed seeds and guards ensure reproducibility and a valid finite (14,3) return.
